Combat announcements and target actions: installed Linux ELF 53.16

Image: ELF:bcc6789e6fb477b785a2b02be80b8b1b054ff88c
Input: native-elf-images.json reference dwarfort, original disk bytes only.
Extraction: tools/extract_combat_announcement_elf.py.
C decompilation: tools/DecompileAdventureAnnouncements.java, Ghidra 12.1.2.
Every native-functions.tsv row has a full elf-source-<start>.c export and
an elf-<role>.asm listing. native-branches.tsv contains all comparisons,
tests and direct branch operands; native-switches.tsv contains 568 decoded
selector destinations across these 33 full unwind owners. Inferred C types
and Ghidra warnings are retained; assembly is authoritative for original
instruction boundaries and cold paths. This is recovered source, not game
output. No game process, desktop, translator sample or test was executed.

The popup, announcement history and timed banner share report.text. Their
wrap/render functions 1160090, 11b2e40 and 1154220 retain report ownership;
the 95-column wrap is a display operation, not a new sentence production.
The same queue also admits dialogue, weather and other reports. Those
producer families remain in adventure-announcement-native and the existing
announcement grammar catalogs; they are not additional combat verbs.

1. Complete unit fields

b6ca30 and b676a0 select native names/identities or appearance/caste/role
captions. A selected name can be authored Latin text, digits or UTF-8; it
need not occur in a procedural-name word list. The complete report's $unit
slot and the target panel's {n} slot first use captured native identity,
then the complete role/name parser, then the existing typed unit resolver.
This handles every such field in attack/defense, damage, wrestling, charge,
collision, item removal, item possession and action/state reports. It adds
no name-specific dictionary entry. $squad retains its separate alias-aware
resolver. Dynamic identities are fields, not finite English literals.

2. Shared damage: 17ebfc0..17f5f78

The actor is a unit, or The [flying |spinning ] ITEM. A normal head consists
of ACTOR, RAW_ATTACK_VERB, TARGET, in the/by the BODY_OR_ITEM, optional from
behind/from the side, optional with EQUIPMENT. A prebuilt head instead
comes from wrestling, collision or bodily impact. Equipment may include a
possessive and an item or anatomical instrument. Unit, body, item, tissue
and material leaves are resolved in their own namespaces.

The complete main outcomes share this head:
  , but it is deflected by EQUIPMENT!
  , but the attack is deflected by EQUIPMENT!
  , lightly tapping the target!
  , but there is no force!
  , but it passes right through!
  , but the attack passes right through!
  , but it glances away!
  , but the attack glances away!
   and the severed part sails off in an arc!
   and LAYER BODY_RESULT!
   and it is mostly cut away from the rest of the torso!
  , DAMAGE_LIST!
   and DAMAGE_LIST!
  !
Failed item/tissue lookups retain the native empty-object productions.
Damage lists compose tearing/tearing apart/shattering/chipping/fracturing/
denting/bruising with complete tissue/body/material fields, comma/and
lists, through-equipment clauses, holes, jamming and breaking-away results.
Auxiliary selector branches retain arteries, nerves, tendons, ligaments,
lodged/latching items, force, interrupted attacks, broken equipment,
stunning, unconsciousness, rage, breathing difficulty, nausea and vomiting.
The finite productions and Chinese wording are the existing scoped rows in
announcement-combat-grammar.tsv, including its empty-field alternatives.
The new typed unit resolution applies throughout that recursive grammar.

3. Other combat producers

199d360: leap/charge, surprise, dodge/scramble/roll/jump, collisions, knockdown,
         tangle/fall and the independent direction/ownership alternatives.
19a1ff0: embedded item pull/twist, possession and stuck-item outcomes.
19a5370: grabs/grips, pinching, gouging, bending, locks, chokeholds, shaking,
         strangling, release and failed escape; shared damage calls retained.
19ad8d0: melee/projectile attack, misses, movement/range, dodge, parry, block,
         deflection and shared hit outcomes; RAW attack verbs and equipment.
1eb5eb0: projectile motion/collision and its typed item/unit destinations.
be81b0/be91f0: force and ground-skid prefixes passed to shared damage.
b8c690: pull out/drop embedded item job.
b92f40/b93fe0: webbing and fireball.
bd1050/bd1780/bd1ff0: breath defense and both fire-breath source owners.
bd2860/bd3550/bd4030/bd4a90/b94a80: cloud/glob/material emissions.
e69120: gain/maintain/lose possession, remains stuck, is torn from anatomy.
78be30: all unit-action report branches, including stands up, mounting,
        dismounting, pushing, struggling in liquids, ammunition loading.

These use the existing combat, adventure-announcement, system and RAW
grammar families. No fixed list of personal names is substituted.
raw-attack-fields.tsv retains current vanilla/installed/available RAW
ATTACK and ATTACK_VERB inputs; raw-procedural-attacks.tsv retains Lua
construction expressions. An available mod file is not evidence that a
world loaded that mod. Body/tissue/item/material suppliers remain typed
dynamic inputs, as in the existing adventure-target-panel RAW inventories.

4. Unit state: c1a160..c2a07d

The producer emits a complete b6ca30 subject, then independently selects
fall/falls + over, regain/regains + consciousness, partial/complete web
freedom, paralysis/sluggishness/numbness/recovery, retching, vomiting with
each medium/destination branch, stun recovery, exhaustion/overexertion,
pain collapse, training changes and five recovered mood states. Arrival,
growth, birth and resident naming use their existing typed grammar paths.
announcement-status-grammar.tsv now gives 34 existing single-unit state
productions the same $unit ownership as combat, including falls over.
Player-only exact sentences keep their existing catalog translations.

5. Target summary and action status: 116e110 and 116bb90

The summary draws an identity, then at most six independent action rows.
Action type selects 0..27; out-of-range/default emits no text:
  0 movement/charging       1 attacking/recovering  2 jumping
  3 holding terrain        4 releasing terrain    5 climbing
  6 working                7 talking              8 regaining balance
  9 parrying              10 blocking             11 dodging
 12 deflection recovery   13 standing up          14 lying down
 15 working               16 pushing object      17 sucking blood
 18 holding item          19 releasing item       20 mounting
 21 dismounting           22 leading animal       23 stop leading animal
 24 loading/nocking ammo  25 shooting weapon      26 throwing item
 27 recovering after shooting

Movement/dodge direction has all eight horizontal directions, upward,
downward and the independently appended above/below qualifiers.
An attack's active timer chooses Attacking versus Recovering from attacking.
A missing target yields that prefix alone. Otherwise the target is you or
the complete b676a0 caption. Reveal flags independently add timing stage
(Remote/Distant/Starting/Incoming/IMMINENT), method (wrestling/grab), an
item or natural attack, attack style and an aiming part. Style bits append
quick/heavy/wild/precise in order, including all combinations. A weapon's
RAW subpart may precede its attack name; NO_SUB omits that subpart. Failed
item lookup emits no instrument. All methods rejoin the common aiming
suffix for active, revealed, valid body targets; explicit wrestling/grab
aiming templates preserve those alternatives before generic unit templates.
Deflection optionally adds a full item; loading selects nocking/loading
and its ammunition field. Exact Chinese wording and typed compositions are
in adventure-target-translations.tsv. The full captured status draw enters
that parser before independent grid fragments; authored unit names remain
valid captures, including when a status has no shortened-source companion.

The combat chooser's prompts, stages, confirmation choices, ratings,
attack styles, wrestling actions and complete dynamic helpers are retained
in adventure-target-panel/elf-decompiled.c and helper-decompiled.txt, plus
this extraction's complete 1182410 owner. Existing panel geometry owns the
whole caption field and removes overlapping generic fragment matches.
